title: Canaries in the Bank: Auditing User-Level Privacy in Private Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2609.13499v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Private Evolution (PE) generates high-fidelity synthetic data in federated settings without exposing users' raw data. It aggregates clipped user votes over a shared candidate bank into a differentially private histogram, with noise calibrated to the worst-case user contribution. However, it is unclear whether an adversary can realize this worst-case privacy loss while following the PE protocol. We introduce a protocol-aware empirical audit in which the server commits to a single shared candidate bank and replaces roughly 1% of its entries with probes derived from a known, non-private canary. We evaluate eight attacks, including an unchanged-bank baseline, exact copies, plausible paraphrases, and high-entropy synthetic nonces. translated_title: 银行中的金丝雀：私有演化中的用户级隐私审计
translated_abstract: 私有演化能够在联邦设置中生成高保真的合成数据，而无需暴露用户的原始数据。它将裁剪后的用户投票聚合到共享候选库上，生成差分隐私直方图，其噪声根据最坏情况下的用户贡献进行校准。然而，尚不清楚对手在遵循PE协议的同时能否真正实现这种最坏情况下的隐私损失。我们提出了一种协议感知的经验审计方法：服务器提交一个单一的共享候选库，并将其约1%的条目替换为从一个已知的、非私有的金丝雀派生出的探测样本。我们评估了八种攻击方式，包括未修改库的基线、精确副本、合理改写以及高熵合成随机数。在Yelp和Sentiment140上的实验表明，自然文本攻击的隐私损失仍远低于理论差分隐私界限，而基于随机数的攻击则获得了强得多的界限，并最接近机制的理论保证。
tldr: 该论文提出一种协议感知的经验隐私审计方法，通过在PE共享候选库中植入金丝雀探测样本并评估八种攻击，发现自然文本攻击的隐私损失远低于理论差分隐私界限，而高熵随机数攻击最接近理论保证。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a protocol-aware empirical privacy audit that plants canary probes into PE's shared candidate bank, showing that natural-text attacks remain well below the theoretical DP bound while high-entropy nonce-based attacks come closest to the mechanism's guarantee.
